newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's Halla in Indonesia cement jv.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's Halla in Indonesia cement jv.

text.p: South Korea's Halla Group said on Tuesday it has agreed in principle to build a joint-venture cement plant in Indonesia.

Halla said in a statement it has signed a memorandum of understanding with the Tadmansori Group of Malaysia and the Ache state government of Indonesia. The construction is scheduled to begin in early 1997 in the Ache state, which is located in northern Sumatra.
The plant is expected to have an annual production capacity of 1.2 million tonnes, which will be exported to Malaysia, Vietnam, the Philippines and other Southeast Asian countries.
Halla will carry out construction of the joint cement plant on a turn-key basis, the statement said.
Other details such as capitalisation of the joint-venture plant are not available at the moment since these are under negotiations between Halla and its foreign partners, it said.
Halla Group is now building a $72 million cement plant in Malaysia's Negeri Sembilan state jointly with a local entity. The plant is expected to produce 1.2 million tonnes a year from late 1997.
